rolls.label: Swat
rolls.note: its attack: fail a roll within its reach and you're swatted

rolls.label: Perception
rolls.note: its own checks only (a Decoy, a surprise); it never rolls to spot you

system.senses: Sees anything in its room not in cover. A sleeper only hears.
system.passive:
Sleeping, distracted, alert or armed with a broom — its Chapter 15 row. You roll against that row's Difficulty; it never rolls to spot you.

RowYour rollNotes
Sleeping HumanStealth (2)Asleep and fine — stay quiet. At Alert 5 they stir; at 7, or Full Alert, they're up and turning on lights.
Distracted HumanStealth (1)On their phone, watching TV. Use the window. It closes.
Alert HumanDeception or Stealth (4)Looking for something. Possibly for you. Do not get spotted.
Human With BroomAthletics (3)The broom has already swung once. Keep moving.
system.escalation: Stirs at 5; up with the lights on at 7 or Full Alert. Its row stays the same.
system.weakness: Its phone, the TV, and a deep conviction that it imagined you.
system.notes:
Note: a glimpse of a spider is “spotted” (+1); loot moving on its own is a confirmed alert (+2). Its reach is the room it's in: fail a roll there, where it can see you, and you're swatted (a hit, Swat 3). A Critical spider it hits ends up under a glass: Out.

No opposed roll: don't pick a Human in the roll dialog's Opposed by list to sneak past it — set the Difficulty from its row instead. Its Perception 3 is only for its own checks, and like any NPC check it needs the full Difficulty.
system.biography:
“Ten Thousand Times Your Size.”

The librarian, the restaurant staff, the cleaning crew and the human who gets up for water: every human in a heist uses this block, at its Chapter 15 Difficulty.
